[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/27 (Sat) 00:34  
[FACT] User is a 32-year-old male.  
[FACT] User has a master's degree in data science from New York University.  
[FACT] User is trying to understand the green card application process, specifically the EB-2 visa category.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The EB-2 visa category is an employment-based, second-preference visa for foreign nationals who possess advanced degrees or exceptional abilities in their field.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To qualify for an EB-2 visa, one must meet one of the following criteria: hold a U.S. master's degree or higher, or demonstrate exceptional ability in their field.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Required documents for EB-2 visa application include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Petition: Your U.S. employer must file a Form I-140, Immigrant Petition for Alien Worker, with USCIS.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Labor Certification: Your employer must obtain a labor certification from the U.S. Department of Labor.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Education and Experience: Provide documentation of your advanced degree, such as a diploma and transcripts, as well as evidence of your relevant work experience.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Letters of Recommendation: Gather letters from experts in your field attesting to your exceptional abilities and achievements.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Resume and CV: Submit a detailed resume and curriculum vitae highlighting your education, work experience, and achievements.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The EB-2 visa application process typically involves the following steps:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Labor Certification: Your employer files a labor certification application with the U.S. Department of Labor.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. I-140 Petition: Your employer files Form I-140 with USCIS, including the approved labor certification and supporting documents.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. I-485 Application: Once the I-140 petition is approved, you can file Form I-485 to adjust your status to a permanent resident or apply for an immigrant visa at a U.S. consulate abroad.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Interview and Approval: Attend an interview at a USCIS office or U.S. consulate, and if approved, receive your green card.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Processing time for EB-2 visa applications can vary, with labor certification taking 6-9 months, I-140 petition taking 3-6 months, and I-485 application taking 6-12 months.
